subject: Specifying different breaks and limits for each facet

messages.author: 1590ee47904628b9
messages.subject: Specifying different breaks and limits for each facet
parts:
Hi,

I am creating a facet plot that has non uniform scaling of the facets
on the x axis. I've set the scales parameter of facet_wrap() to
'free_x'
and would like to adjust the breaks and limits for the x scale
separately
for each individual facet, using scale_x_continuous(). Is it possible
to
do this?

Thanks,

Kevin

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: Re: Specifying different breaks and limits for each facet
parts:
And also, if you're using different axis labels for each facet, maybe
you don't want a faceted graph? Maybe you want separate graphs with
separate data (or subsets of the data)? You can always put multiple
graphs in a single figure. Section 8.4.2 of Hadley's book shows how to
do this with grid_layout() and viewport().

-Harlan

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Specifying different breaks and limits for each facet
parts:
Hi,

I wonder whether it would be possible (desirable?) to define a
widthDetails.ggplot2 method (and heightDetails) so that grid knows the
size of the legend object.

Consider the following case,

library(ggplot2)
p <- qplot(data = mtcars, mpg, hp, geom = "point",
colour = cyl)
p1 <- p + opts(legend.position = "none")
p2 <- qplot(data = mtcars, wt, disp, geom = "point",
colour = cyl) + opts(legend.position = "none")
legend <- p + opts(keep = "legend_box")


legend <- ggplotGrob(legend)
top <- ggplotGrob(p1)
bottom <- ggplotGrob(p2)


layout <- grid.layout(nrow = 2, ncol = 1)

gf = grid.frame(name="gf", layout=layout)

grid.place("gf", top, row=1, col=1)
grid.place("gf", bottom, row=2, col=1)
grid.pack("gf", legend, side="right")

The space allocated by grid.pack clearly doesn't understand that only
the legend is to be drawn (in fact, I'm not sure how it infers the
size of a ggplotGrob at all).


All the best,

baptiste
